failure_modes: Selecting a dose edit (C001/C003) without evidence of a wrong direction or weak dose would add unnecessary coordinate displacement and noncore squared-displacement energy with no demonstrated affinity gain.
Selecting a schedule edit (C005/C006) would impose an early/late allocation not supported by the descriptive, non-extrapolable contrast curves, risking surrounding-coordinate displacement and strain.
Treating the observed-node contrast trends as validated temporal recipes or as spatial gradients would be an unsupported inference; they are descriptive diagnostics over the observed window only.
No decoded terminal affinity labels or final predicted affinity outcomes are available to this role, so no edit can be justified on affinity benefit.
rationale: D1.2: The Analyst's temporal evidence is descriptive only. The continuous contrast curves are observed-node linear fits with polynomial_accepted false, extrapolation_allowed false, and relative node RMSE ~0.29-0.78 (F004), so they are not validated temporal recipes and cannot be compiled into a teacher-coordinate or regional-attention change. No registered temporal recipe is confirmed to express the non-monotone landmark soft-mass / local displacement contrast (H001 falsifier), and the opposing first/last rate z-values with multiple sign changes reject a single signed whole-window contrast (H002). The only offered choices are dose (native_rms_ratio C001-C003) and schedule (time_ramp_power C004-C006) parameters; neither changes teacher coordinates or regional attention, so no time-conditioned alternative is available to select. D3.1: Delivery diagnostics show mean_delivered_over_calibration ~0.330 with backtrack_fraction 0.0, cap_active_fraction 0.0 and zero_injection_fraction 0.0 across all observed nodes and batches, i.e. the incumbent dose is delivered cleanly with no clipping or backtracking and no evidence of a wrong direction or a weak dose. There is no evidence-based reason to move native_rms_ratio off the incumbent 0.33 (C002), and whole-reward rescaling canceled by normalization would not be an effective dose edit. D3.2: The incumbent time_ramp_power is 0.0 (C004), a fixed schedule over the full learned support [0.0,0.5]; the temporal evidence is descriptive and does not establish an early/late allocation advantage, so the fixed schedule is retained. D4.1: The incumbent is the supplied static endpoint-pointcloud program with native_rms_ratio 0.33 and time_ramp_power 0.0; the Analyst evidence provides no defensible expected advantage for any offered edit, so retaining the incumbent is the correct choice. D4.2: A concrete failure response to an unsupported dose or schedule edit would be unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates (noncore squared-displacement energy) and possible strain/clash, with no demonstrated affinity benefit; because the objective is affinity-first and no decoded terminal affinity outcome is supplied, this predicted failure further supports retaining the incumbent. Temperatures are immutable and are not edited.
